description:
Proposal page first, no build. The distiller creates and kills 18.2 million off-heap binary stubs on 32,000 lines (about 560 per input line); each is a 32-byte ProcBin holding its own SharedBin reference, pushed on the MSO chain by alloc_procbin, and the sweep must visit every dead one (mso_unreached_closures and mso_sweep each walk the young chain: two walks per collection). On the full log fz_bs_read_binary_ref is 17% of samples, alloc_bitstring_suffix 4%, alloc_procbin 3%, the two chain walks 4%.
Page compares, with spikes and predictions: (a) a view of an on-heap binary points at that binary instead of holding a SharedBin reference (BEAM sub-binary), so a dead view is never swept; (b) a self-recursive match passes its position instead of building a rest (BEAM match-context reuse; see the fz-sc8.183 page, Not in this ticket); (c) resource stubs on their own chain so the destructor search does not walk binary stubs (proposed on the fz-sc8.184 page, not built). Includes a removal ledger.

comments.text:
Step 0 spike result (throwaway worktree, build path only, behind a switch, nothing landed; patch kept in session scratch as cursor/spike-cursor.patch + spike_cursor.rs).
Walk over 168 MB: 27.2 -> 15.7 ns/byte (predicted ~14); 129.7G -> 85.1G instructions; 32 -> 0 bytes allocated per byte; from-space collected 5.66 GB -> 24 MB; collections 125,829 -> 10,912 (predicted <10: every scheduler yield collects, each copying 64-128 bytes).
Remaining walk cost: acc + c through a continuation (fz-sc8.197) ~58% of samples; fz_mark_published_ref_aliased 10%, unexplained.
Decoder under the spike: 6% MORE instructions (28.8G -> 30.6G on 32,000 lines), output identical. The spike converts binary<->cursor at each function's edge; it applied only to skip_ws/digits/fraction_digits/exponent_digits (short loops), not to val/string/object/array, whose rest goes to another function or returns in {:ok, v, rest}.
Design consequences: (1) the cursor must cross calls and returns or it is a loss on the decoder, so a per-function conversion must not land alone; (2) a parameter typed binary|cursor travels boxed and gains nothing: the cursor must be the parameter's one layout, chosen by demand; (3) the position advance must be inline arithmetic, not a Kernel.+ call (that made the walk slower: 150G instructions).

The 10% fz_mark_published_ref_aliased in the spike profile is explained: Prim::Share emits it unless the value's kind is known not to be a list (native_codegen/prim.rs); it only marks list spines. The spike's source lane was an untyped AnyRef. A real cursor lane is a known binary, so the call is not emitted.

Walkthrough notes 1 (census of lib/json.fz against the page's rule 'any other use joins to Whole'):
- The body IR already carries a match as (source, pos): LoweredStep::BitstringRead {value, next, source, pos, spec}; the rest r::binary is one such read. A cursor is that pair left unbuilt. Demand for reads is noted in runtime_demand.rs (BitstringRead arm ~2168 notes source Whole when value is live; note_clause_matcher_demands ~2321).
- The absorbing rule does NOT serve the decoder. string/3's hot clause passes r on, but cold clauses use the same parameter whole: {:error, b} (escapes as any), and run_join does byte_size(s) - byte_size(b). Under 'Whole absorbs', b is Whole and the per-byte rest stays.
- So the rule has to be: a binary that some consumer matches travels as a cursor; a consumer that needs the binary makes it whole at that use (pos == 0 gives the source itself, no allocation). byte_size / bit_size / comparison with a literal are answered from the cursor without building.
- Risk of that rule: a cursor used whole at k sites on one path allocates k stubs where today it allocates 1. Needs a measurement, and a dedupe within one body.
- Returns: {:ok, v, r} | {:error, any} flows through array_item/object_key/object_value whose second clause passes the tuple on whole (other -> other). If that boxes the tuple today, r is made whole once per JSON value (per token, not per byte). To verify: how a union-of-tuples return is demanded today.
- Pairs that already work as nested demand: digits returns {acc, b} matched by fraction({whole, <<".", r>>}) -> TupleFields([Whole, Matched]).
Still to read before the walkthrough: transport layout_from_demand, dispatch bit reads at a base position (lower_bitstring_region), interp path.

Walkthrough notes 2 (page is version 2):
- Probe (#585 base, release): loop/item over a 1,048,576-byte binary with v returning {:ok, 1, r} | {:error, b} allocates 1,048,576 tuples (struct_allocs), also when both consumer clauses destructure. A two-shape tuple return is boxed today, so its rest must be whole: one stub per token. One-shape returns ({acc, b} from digits) travel as fields.
- Layout hook: layout_from_demand (jobs/transport.rs ~2581) matches on ShapeDemand; ShapeDescr has Nothing | Lane | Tuple | Callable; a Cursor variant is two lanes whose boxing is a suffix binary, not a tuple. ShapeDescr::Tuple is handled in jobs/native.rs, jobs/transport.rs, canon.rs, ir_interp/backend.rs (16 sites in native+interp).
- Dispatch hook: lower_bitstring_region (jobs/native.rs ~3764) reads BitstringBitLen(subject) and starts pos at Const 0; with a cursor subject it starts at the position lane.
- Per input line of h32000 (first 4000 lines): 418 bytes, 30.4 strings (270 bytes), 7.9 numbers, 27.3 values, 6.05 objects, 2.06 arrays. Predicted stubs per line: ~560 today -> ~140 (4 per string: returned rest, run slice, two byte_size in run_join) -> ~80 with byte_size answered from the cursor.
- Join rule proposed: Matched join Whole = Matched (whole made at the use; pos 0 gives the source); Matched join TupleFields = Whole. Awaiting the user's decision.

Experiment E-count (running; predictions written before the data): execution counters on every site that builds a binary field through the runtime, in the built distiller on 32,000 lines, split rest / non-rest and by function.
 Q1: rest reads are 400-450 per input line (418 bytes per line; one rest per byte matched), non-rest binary reads about 30-60 per line.
 Q2: under the version 1 rule (any whole use cancels the cursor) the rests that go are only those in functions with no whole use of the parameter (digits, fraction_digits, exponent_digits, skip_ws): under 10% of executed rest reads.
 Q3: under the version 2 rule (whole made at the use) at least 85% of executed rest reads go: everything in string/3's plain-byte clause and the number loops; what stays is about one per token.
 Q4: string/3's plain-byte clause alone is over half of all executed rest reads.
If Q2 is wrong (v1 already removes most), the simpler absorbing rule is enough and version 2's trade-off is not needed.

E-count result (distiller, 32,000 lines, 20.66 MB = 645 bytes per line; my 418 was the first 4,000 lines only). Binary fields built through the runtime: 21,795,877; rests 20,296,109 (634 per line); non-rest 1,499,768.
 Q1 missed on the absolute (634 per line, predicted 400-450) because of the sample; it is about one rest per input byte as expected.
 Q4 held: JSON.string/3 builds 14,576,217 rests (71.8%); its plain-byte clause alone 13,099,663 (64.5%).
 Q2 held: under the version 1 rule only digits (1,308,642) and skip_ws (32,000) lose their rests: 6.6%. Every other matcher has a clause that uses the parameter whole ({:error, b}) or passes it to one that does.
 Q3 missed: under version 2 the rests still built are about 5.4M (73% removed, predicted 85%): 1,476,554 stored in string's {:ok, run, r}; about 2,953,396 made whole only so run_join can ask byte_size(s) and byte_size(b); about 515,774 at a number's {:ok, n, b}; about 300,000 at object/array ends; about 150,000 at literals. With byte_size answered from the cursor: about 2.44M built, 88% removed (169 -> 76 per line).
 So: the absorbing rule is not enough (6.6%); version 2 is needed; byte_size on a cursor is worth 15 points and belongs in the unit, not after it.

User approved the page (version 2 with counts) on 2026-11-14: join rule v2 (Matched joined with Whole is Matched; Matched joined with TupleFields is Whole), byte_size answered from the cursor inside this unit, and two-shape returns as fields filed as fz-sc8.220. Base: PR #600 (the splice), because byte_size on a cursor needs byte_size inline at the call site. Worktree ../fz-sc8-183, branch fz-sc8.208/cursor.

title: A binary that is only taken apart travels as its source and a position
